narrativeReportMd:
# EpisodeOfCare R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
The resource identity is stable, but local element changes are breaking. The highest-impact issues are `patient` -> `subject`, `diagnosis.condition` changing to repeating `CodeableReference`, the semantic split between reasons and diagnoses, removal of `diagnosis.rank`, and `team` -> `careTeam`.

## Scope
This report covers the base EpisodeOfCare StructureDefinition and selected local terminology/datatype dependencies. Inherited base-artifact differences are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration requires explicit transforms, not version relabeling. R6 can represent Group subjects, code-only or multiple diagnosis conditions, separate reasons for care, non-Condition reason targets, multiple diagnosis uses, and Account-based diagnosis sequencing; several are lossy when exported to R4.

## Follow-up analysis
Coordinate with CodeableReference, Account, Resource, and DomainResource reports for shared conversion and inherited-base issues.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `EpisodeOfCare` has hard local breaks despite stable canonical identity. Top concerns are subject renaming, diagnosis CodeableReference reshaping, and reason/diagnosis semantic split. Main uncertainty is official rationale and preferred migration guidance for diagnosis role/rank.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Apply explicit property renames, wrap old diagnosis Condition references as R6 CodeableReference arrays, classify old diagnosis data into reason/diagnosis/both, and decide how to preserve billing rank via Account or extensions. Backward conversion is lossy for Group subjects, code-only CodeableReferences, non-Condition reasons, and multiple diagnosis uses.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: High confidence for structural deltas from direct StructureDefinition comparison. Medium confidence for intent and terminology normalization because official narrative diffs, Jira notes, and full terminology expansions were not supplied.

findings.title: Required patient was renamed to required subject and widened to Patient or Group

semanticText.short: The patient who is the focus of this episode of care
semanticText.definition: The patient who is the focus of this episode of care.

newState.summary: R6 requires EpisodeOfCare.subject as Reference(Patient or Group).

semanticText.short: The patient/group who is the focus of this episode of care
semanticText.definition: The patient/group who is the focus of this episode of care.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements have the same required cardinality and workflow mapping (`Event.subject`), with R6 generalizing patient to subject.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 resources with `patient` are missing required R6 `subject` and contain an unknown property. R6 Group subjects cannot be represented in R4 `patient` without an extension or rejection.

justification.inferredGoal: Align EpisodeOfCare with generic workflow subject naming and allow group-focused episodes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `patient` element, broaden its target to Patient or Group, and clarify that it represents the workflow subject.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing Group-focused episodes and aligning with workflow subject semantics are reasonable goals, but the required wire-name rename breaks essentially every R4 EpisodeOfCare instance. Because R4 `patient` already mapped to `Event.subject`, R6 could have widened and redefined that same element rather than requiring `subject`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would retain `EpisodeOfCare.patient` as `1..1 Reference(Patient | Group)` with updated short and definition text explaining that it is the patient or group subject. This preserves R4-valid Patient references while supporting Group subjects. The tradeoff is lasting semantic debt in the element name; adding both `patient` and `subject` would be worse because duplicate same-resource representations could conflict and persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances without duplicate fields, but leaves a misleading `patient` name for Group subjects and weaker alignment with workflow naming.

evidence.detail: R4 defines required `patient` targeting Patient.
R6 defines required `subject` targeting Patient and Group.
R4 maps to workflow Event.subject.
R6 maps to workflow Event.subject.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are minimal; the R4-to-R6 transform is a field rename, while Group subjects require a backport policy.

findings.narrativeMd: The required focus element changed identity from `patient` to `subject`. This breaks strict JSON validation, generated model properties, and FHIRPath expressions, even though the clinical role is recognizable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid R4 instances with `patient` are new-invalid until transformed. Patient subjects can round-trip by renaming, but R6 Group subjects are not native R4 EpisodeOfCare content.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move R4 `patient` to R6 `subject` unchanged. For R6-to-R4, map only Patient subjects directly; use an extension, rejection, or profile-specific transform for Group subjects. Test both target types.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was partly avoidable: retaining `patient` as deprecated would preserve old wire format but create duplicate ways to represent the same subject.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a required element wire-name change, not only a broadened reference target. An R4 `EpisodeOfCare` instance carrying `patient` must be transformed before it is a conformant R6 instance, and generated clients, FHIRPath expressions, and mappings that use `patient` need code changes. Supporting Group-focused episodes is reasonable, but the same mandatory subject slot is central enough that retaining the old path with updated semantics looks like a plausible lower-disruption base design.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-EpisodeOfCare snapshot `EpisodeOfCare.patient`: 1..1 Reference(Patient), mapped to workflow `Event.subject`.
R6 StructureDefinition-EpisodeOfCare snapshot `EpisodeOfCare.subject`: 1..1 Reference(Patient|Group), also mapped to workflow `Event.subject`.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral: it does not create normative stability pressure, but it also does not soften a required central field rename into a minor concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON with `patient` lacks required R6 `subject`; generated models and FHIRPath paths change. R6 Group subjects also create an R6-to-R4 loss case.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `EpisodeOfCare.patient` as the required Reference and widened it to Patient or Group with updated wording and aliases. The tradeoff is semantic/name debt because `patient` is awkward for Group subjects and less aligned with workflow naming, but it would preserve the common R4 wire shape without introducing duplicate fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and less-breaking-alternative-Yes assessment; the fresh rationale emphasizes the required central path rename rather than whole-resource burden.

findings.title: diagnosis.condition changed from one required Reference to repeating CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 required exactly one Reference(Condition) per diagnosis.

semanticText.definition: A list of conditions/problems/diagnoses that this episode of care is intended to be providing care for.

newState.summary: R6 allows zero or more CodeableReference(Condition) values.

semanticText.definition: The medical condition that was addressed during the episode of care, expressed as a text, code or a reference to another resource.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path is unchanged, but datatype, cardinality, binding, and semantic text changed locally.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 serializes a single Reference object. R6 serializes an array of CodeableReference objects, nesting a reference under `condition[].reference`. R6 can also carry code-only, multiple, or absent condition values that R4 cannot faithfully represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow diagnosis conditions to be expressed by code/text or by Condition reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `diagnosis.condition` Reference and add a new optional repeating CodeableReference sibling for coded, text, or multiple conditions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of representing diagnoses by text, code, or Condition reference is reasonable, and CodeableReference gives one coherent model for those cases. A less-breaking design exists, but it would split the same diagnosis fact across old Reference and new codeable fields and require rules for precedence, duplication, and consistency.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would leave `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.condition` as the R4 `Reference(Condition)` and add a new repeated element such as `conditionCodeableReference` for code-only, text-only, and multiple conditions. That is more than conversion guidance and would preserve R4 instances, but it is incomplete and costly: R6 producers could populate either or both locations, validators would need conflict rules, and deprecated same-resource representations might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 references, but creates overlapping same-resource condition representations with conflict and indefinite-deprecation risk.

evidence.detail: R4 is 1..1 Reference targeting Condition.
R6 is 0..* CodeableReference targeting Condition with condition-code example binding.
CodeableReference contains child `reference` of type Reference.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 Reference must be wrapped as a CodeableReference array item. Code-only or multiple R6 values are lossy for R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `diagnosis.condition` is a major local break: the element path remains but its JSON shape, type, and multiplicity changed. Existing R4 diagnosis fragments will not validate as R6 without structural wrapping.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is old-valid/new-invalid for common R4 instances with diagnosis. R6-to-R4 is only direct when there is exactly one CodeableReference containing a Condition Reference; concept-only, multiple, or missing conditions need policy.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each R4 Reference as one R6 CodeableReference item. For backport, create Condition resources, use extensions, reject unsupported cases, or define a lossy mapping explicitly. Test reference, concept-only, multiple, and omitted cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less disruptive design could preserve the old Reference and add a separate codeable choice. That would retain wire compatibility but complicate the R6 model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `diagnosis.condition` changes from a single Condition Reference object to a repeating CodeableReference array. R4 diagnosis entries therefore need structural wrapping, and R6 can express concept-only, text-only, multiple, or absent conditions that do not fit the R4 one-reference shape. Still, the R6 model has a coherent goal: representing diagnosis conditions by code/text or by resource reference in one datatype. The lower-break alternatives create parallel representations of the same clinical fact.
keyEvidence: R4 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.condition`: 1..1 Reference(Condition).
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.condition`: 0..* CodeableReference(Condition) with an example `condition-code` binding.
R6 CodeableReference contains optional `concept` and optional `reference` children.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the judgment is driven by the concrete JSON-shape break and the modeling tradeoff, not by a high or low maturity presumption.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid with R6-to-R4 loss: an R4 Reference at `diagnosis.condition` is not the R6 array-of-CodeableReference shape, while R6 concept-only or multiple conditions cannot be represented faithfully as one R4 Condition reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained the R4 Reference field and added a new repeating coded/text condition field, but that would split one diagnosis condition across overlapping fields and require precedence, duplication, and consistency rules. That is a material base-model cost, so it is not a clearly better design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and Partial alternative assessment; the break is real, but the fresh judgment treats the CodeableReference redesign as proportionate.

findings.title: R4 diagnosis semantics split between R6 reason and diagnosis

oldState.summary: R4 diagnosis covered diagnoses relevant to, or intended for, the episode.

semanticText.short: The list of diagnosis relevant to this episode of care

newState.summary: R6 adds reason for expected reasons and describes diagnosis as addressed medical conditions.

semanticText.short: The list of medical reasons that are expected to be addressed during the episode of care
semanticText.comment: R6 diagnosis says conditions actually addressed may also appear in reason if they were provided as reasons.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 preserved `diagnosis` but changed its meaning while adding a new `reason` backbone that overlaps with R4 intended-reason wording.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Even after syntax conversion, blindly mapping R4 diagnosis to R6 diagnosis can assert that a condition was addressed; mapping it only to reason can lose treated-diagnosis information. R6 reason can also contain non-Condition references or coded concepts with no R4 slot.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate why an episode is expected from what was actually addressed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `reason` while retaining the broader R4 `diagnosis` semantics, or add a new addressed-diagnosis element while deprecating the old broad meaning.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating expected reasons from conditions actually addressed is clinically meaningful and can reduce downstream ambiguity. The breakage is partly semantic rather than only syntactic: old R4 diagnosis data may not say whether an item was merely a reason, actually addressed, or both. Less-breaking designs are possible, but they materially compromise the clean separation R6 appears to be pursuing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: One partial alternative would introduce the optional R6 `reason` backbone while leaving `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis` with its R4 broad relevant-or-intended meaning. Another would keep the old broad element deprecated and add a new addressed-diagnosis element. Either would preserve more historical data without forcing immediate classification, but R6 consumers could no longer rely on `diagnosis` meaning conditions actually addressed, and duplicate or overlapping reason/diagnosis fields could accumulate.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces migration ambiguity for old data, but weakens the new reason-versus-addressed distinction or creates overlapping clinical representations.

evidence.detail: R4 condition text says the episode is intended to provide care for the condition.
R6 adds reason for medical reasons expected to be addressed.
R6 diagnosis comment distinguishes addressed conditions from reasons.
R6 reason.value supports CodeableReference targets beyond Condition.

examples.examplesMd: Some R4 diagnoses should become reason, some diagnosis, and some both. Non-Condition or code-only R6 reasons have no native R4 equivalent.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a clinically important split: `reason` is what is expected to be addressed, while `diagnosis` is what was addressed. This is a semantic migration risk separate from the structural type changes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The split can produce behaviorally wrong but syntactically valid R6 if all R4 diagnosis data is placed in the wrong bucket. R6-to-R4 may need to merge reason and diagnosis and lose the distinction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify old diagnosis entries using clinical state, claims data, or business rules. Populate `reason`, `diagnosis`, or both deliberately. Backport non-Condition reasons through extensions, related resources, or rejection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split is likely justified by semantic clarity. It could have been less disruptive with a compatibility extension, explicit ConceptMap-like guidance, or a deprecation period.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The path-level risk is semantic misclassification: R4 diagnosis text described conditions the episode was intended to address, while R6 separates expected reasons from conditions actually addressed. A migration that blindly sends all old diagnosis data to only one R6 bucket can overstate treatment or lose the reason-for-care meaning. That requires clinical or business judgment in some cases, but the R6 distinction is useful and computable, and compatibility-preserving alternatives weaken or duplicate that distinction.
keyEvidence: R4 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.condition` definition: conditions/problems/diagnoses the episode is intended to provide care for.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.reason` definition and comment: medical reasons expected to be addressed during the episode.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis` definition and comment: medical conditions actually addressed; a condition may appear in both reason and diagnosis.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.reason.value`: CodeableReference targets include Condition, DiagnosticReport, Procedure, Observation, and HealthcareService.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. It does not by itself demand old broad semantics be preserved, but the review still counts expert-dependent clinical mapping as real migration work.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation with R6-to-R4 loss: structurally valid transforms can carry the wrong meaning, and R6 non-Condition or concept-only reasons have no native R4 EpisodeOfCare diagnosis slot.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have added `reason` while leaving `diagnosis` with the broader R4 meaning, or kept the broad field deprecated and added a new addressed-diagnosis field. Those designs preserve more legacy ambiguity, but they undermine the clean reason-versus-addressed separation and create overlapping clinical representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact and Partial alternative assessment; I agree the migration risk is significant, but I characterize the primary mechanism as semantic/expert mapping rather than a direct hard validation break.

findings.title: diagnosis.role was replaced by repeating diagnosis.use with a different preferred ValueSet

oldState.summary: R4 had optional single role CodeableConcept with preferred diagnosis-role binding.

binding.description: The type of diagnosis this condition represents.

newState.summary: R6 has optional repeating use CodeableConcept with preferred encounter-diagnosis-use binding.

binding.description: The type of diagnosis this condition represents.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short text is nearly identical, but the path, cardinality, and preferred terminology changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `role` are structurally invalid in R6. The binding is preferred rather than required, but R4 diagnosis-role codes do not have a one-to-one semantic map to R6 working/final and R6 allows multiple uses.

justification.inferredGoal: Move diagnosis classification to encounter-style use and allow multiple uses.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `diagnosis.role`, widen it to repeat, and update or prefer the encounter diagnosis use terminology without changing the wire name.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of supporting encounter-style working/final uses and multiple classifications is reasonable, but the path rename from `role` to `use` is not necessary to achieve it. The element remains a CodeableConcept with essentially the same definition, and changing a preferred binding or increasing max cardinality can be done without invalidating the R4 wire property.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would keep `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.role` as `0..* CodeableConcept`, update the short/definition if needed, and bind it preferentially to the encounter diagnosis use ValueSet or to a transition ValueSet that includes the new use codes. Existing R4 codings would remain structurally valid because the binding is preferred rather than required. The main tradeoff is a less harmonized name than `use` and weaker pressure to normalize legacy role codes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances, but keeps older `role` naming and permits legacy diagnosis-role codings under a preferred binding, slowing terminology convergence.

evidence.detail: R4 `role` is 0..1 CodeableConcept bound preferred to diagnosis-role.
R6 `use` is 0..* CodeableConcept bound preferred to encounter-diagnosis-use.
R4 diagnosis-role codes include AD, DD, CC, CM, pre-op, post-op, and billing.
R6 encounter-diagnosis-use codes are working and final.

examples.examplesMd: Forward migration can wrap old role as a use array, but normalized code translation requires a terminology decision.

findings.narrativeMd: `diagnosis.role` changed name, multiplicity, and preferred terminology. This affects validation when `role` is present, generated code, and semantic normalization of diagnosis classifications.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The field rename is a hard instance break. The terminology change is primarily semantic because the binding remains preferred. R6-to-R4 is lossy for multiple uses and for working/final without a chosen R4 role equivalent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `role` to `use` and wrap as an array. Preserve original codings, add mapped R6 codings if a ConceptMap is approved, and decide how to collapse multiple R6 uses for R4 export.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping `role` as deprecated while adding `use` would have reduced breakage but left two overlapping diagnosis classification fields.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The element remains an optional CodeableConcept with essentially the same role/use description, but the wire path changes from `role` to `use`, the max cardinality widens, and the preferred ValueSet changes. Because preferred bindings do not make old codings structurally invalid, the hard break is mainly the rename. Supporting multiple working/final uses could plausibly have been done without changing the R4 property name.
keyEvidence: R4 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.role`: 0..1 CodeableConcept, preferred binding to `ValueSet/diagnosis-role`.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.use`: 0..* CodeableConcept, preferred binding to `ValueSet/encounter-diagnosis-use`.
R4 diagnosis-role CodeSystem concepts include AD, DD, CC, CM, pre-op, post-op, and billing.
R6 encounter-diagnosis-use CodeSystem concepts are working and final.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; it permits evolution, but an avoidable field rename on otherwise similar content still deserves scrutiny.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: an R4 `diagnosis.role` property is not recognized at the R6 path, and generated code or FHIRPath rules using `role` must change. The terminology change is mostly semantic/conformance pressure because the binding remains preferred.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.role`, widened it to repeat, and updated the preferred binding or used a transition ValueSet. The cost is retaining the older `role` name and allowing legacy codings longer, but it would preserve R4 instances and still support multiple classifications.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact and less-breaking-alternative-Yes assessment; I would separate the structural rename from the weaker preferred-binding terminology pressure.

findings.title: diagnosis.rank was removed from EpisodeOfCare

oldState.summary: R4 had optional single diagnosis.rank positiveInt.

semanticText.short: Ranking of the diagnosis (for each role type)
semanticText.definition: Ranking of the diagnosis (for each role type).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 EpisodeOfCare comments point billing diagnoses to Account, and R6 Account has `Account.diagnosis.sequence`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R6 EpisodeOfCare element preserves rank/sequence semantics; Account contains the related billing sequence path.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using `diagnosis.rank` contain an undefined R6 property, and the ranking data has no same-resource destination. Silent dropping can lose billing or prioritization information.

justification.inferredGoal: Move billing diagnosis sequencing out of EpisodeOfCare and into Account.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `diagnosis.rank` as deprecated while directing billing sequencing to `Account.diagnosis.sequence`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving billing-oriented diagnosis sequencing to Account is a reasonable modeling goal, especially because R6 Account has an explicit diagnosis sequence. However, removing the same-resource field creates a hard R4-to-R6 data-loss risk for existing ranks. The less-breaking base alternative is real but has material interoperability and reconciliation costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base R6 design would keep `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.rank` as a deprecated `0..1 positiveInt` with a comment that billing ranking should use `Account.diagnosis.sequence`. That would preserve R4-valid instances without relying only on migration tooling. The tradeoff is substantial: rank could be duplicated between EpisodeOfCare and Account, stale values could conflict, and reimbursement-related sequencing might remain split indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old EpisodeOfCare data, but leaves competing EpisodeOfCare and Account ranking locations that could diverge and persist.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `diagnosis.rank` as 0..1 positiveInt.
R6 EpisodeOfCare has no `diagnosis.rank`.
R6 says billing diagnoses can be documented on Account resources which support ranking.
R6 Account has diagnosis.sequence 0..1 positiveInt.

examples.examplesMd: The Account example is illustrative; it is not a same-resource EpisodeOfCare transform.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 ranking on EpisodeOfCare diagnosis is gone. This is a hard break for records that used it and a data-loss risk unless migration handles the apparent move of billing-oriented sequencing to Account.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old instances with `diagnosis.rank` are new-invalid. R6 EpisodeOfCare has no rank to backport, but R6 Account may carry related sequence data outside this resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 records with rank. If it is billing sequence, migrate with the diagnosis to R6 Account.diagnosis.sequence; otherwise preserve with an extension or profile-specific rule. Do not silently drop it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal is probably model-cleanup toward Account, but retaining a deprecated rank would have made same-resource migration lossless.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This optional field is removed from EpisodeOfCare with no same-resource replacement. R6 points billing-oriented diagnosis sequencing toward Account, which is a plausible target model, but migration is not a simple field rename: an implementer must decide whether the old rank was billing sequence, create or locate the relevant Account context, or preserve non-billing priority some other way. Because rank can affect reimbursement or prioritization and a deprecated transitional field would preserve old instances, this merits renewed design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.rank`: 0..1 positiveInt, defined as ranking of the diagnosis for each role type.
R6 StructureDefinition-EpisodeOfCare has no `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis.rank` element.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.diagnosis` comment says billing diagnoses can be documented on Account resources that support ranking.
R6 `Account.diagnosis.sequence`: 0..1 positiveInt for diagnosis ranking.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but billing- or priority-related data loss is a concrete business risk that is not erased by trial-use status.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid with R4-to-R6 data-loss risk: R4 instances containing `diagnosis.rank` have an undefined R6 property, and the related Account sequence is outside the EpisodeOfCare resource and requires policy-driven migration.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial but credible. R6 could have retained `diagnosis.rank` as deprecated with guidance to use `Account.diagnosis.sequence` for billing. The tradeoff is duplicate or stale ranking information across EpisodeOfCare and Account, but a transitional base element would materially reduce same-resource data loss.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact and Partial alternative assessment; I place more weight on billing/priority data loss and therefore judge the finding as Revisit.

findings.title: team was renamed to careTeam

oldState.summary: R4 had optional repeating team Reference(CareTeam).

newState.summary: R6 has optional repeating careTeam Reference(CareTeam).

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements share cardinality, type, target, short text, definition, alias, and workflow mapping.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Instances using R4 `team` are invalid in R6 until renamed. Data conversion is otherwise deterministic because target and cardinality did not change.

justification.inferredGoal: Use an element name matching the referenced CareTeam resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `team` element and clarify or alias it as the CareTeam reference instead of renaming the wire property.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new `careTeam` name is clearer, but this is otherwise a pure rename: cardinality, datatype, target profile, and mapping are unchanged. A base R6 wire rename for clarity alone is difficult to justify when the old element could have been retained with updated narrative or aliases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `EpisodeOfCare.team` as `0..* Reference(CareTeam)` and add clearer definition text, comments, or alias metadata explaining that it references the care team. This preserves all R4 instances and avoids duplicate fields. Adding `careTeam` alongside deprecated `team` would also be less breaking, but it would introduce unnecessary duplicate same-resource representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids validation and code-generation break with minimal cost; only persistent name inconsistency and less harmonized path naming remain.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `team` as 0..* Reference(CareTeam).
R6 defines `careTeam` as 0..* Reference(CareTeam).
R4 maps to Event.performer.actor.
R6 maps to Event.performer.actor.

examples.examplesMd: Move the array unchanged between `team` and `careTeam`.

findings.narrativeMd: `team` to `careTeam` is a straightforward local rename, but it still breaks strict validators, generated properties, and path-based extraction rules.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid instances with `team` are new-invalid. R6 `careTeam` values can be represented in R4 by reversing the rename; no target or cardinality loss was found.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `team` to `careTeam` for R4-to-R6 and reverse for R6-to-R4. Update generated-code references, FHIRPath paths, and tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been fully backward compatible with a deprecated alias. The chosen design favors clearer naming.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a pure path rename for an optional repeating CareTeam reference: cardinality, target resource, and workflow mapping are unchanged. Migration is mechanically reversible, so the practical risk is lower than for diagnosis or subject, but strict validators, generated properties, and path-based extraction still break when `team` is present. A clarity-only rename with a simple keep-the-old-name alternative is disproportionate even for FMM 2 content.
keyEvidence: R4 `EpisodeOfCare.team`: 0..* Reference(CareTeam), alias `CareTeam`, mapped to workflow `Event.performer.actor`.
R6 `EpisodeOfCare.careTeam`: 0..* Reference(CareTeam), alias `CareTeam`, mapped to workflow `Event.performer.actor`.
R6 adds explanatory care-team comments but does not change the reference target or cardinality.
R4 maturity map: EpisodeOfCare is trial-use, FMM 2.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. The optional and non-summary nature lowers practical severity, but it does not justify a low-value wire rename when the old shape could have been preserved.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with `team` are not valid R6 at that path, and code or FHIRPath expressions using `EpisodeOfCare.team` must be renamed.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `EpisodeOfCare.team` and improved the definition, comments, or alias metadata to clarify that it references CareTeam. The main tradeoff is a less explicit path name; adding a parallel `careTeam` field would be less attractive because it creates duplicate same-resource representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact and less-breaking-alternative-Yes assessment; the fresh review emphasizes that the impact is narrow but the base-model rename appears avoidable.
